text:
alex: quick heads-up — observed a weird oscillation after yesterday's kernel switch when deploy-time warmers run 
alex: cold-cache hit-rate spiked briefly but overall tail latency for prefill jobs went up ~30ms on p99
mira: ugh, any traces?
alex: pasting trimmed perf snippet and config we used:
```
# prefill job config
warmer_type: synthetic
qps: 250
batch_target_ms: 20
kernel_hint: auto
prefill_ttl_s: 300
```
perf: kernel selector chose small-kernel path for most requests (seq len small) -> poor throughput on GPU, KV store looked fine but many keys missed due to prefix normalization change
denise: prefix normalization change? that's the new deterministic keying from last sprint right?
alex: yup — we started hashing prompt prefixes after stripping punctuation. that reduced cardinality for real traffic but the synthetic warmers generate many short toy prefixes so collisions + TTL churn caused lower effective hit-rate
mira: what are metrics? hit-rate / key-churn numbers?
alex: comparing 4h window pre/post switch:
- real traffic hit-rate: 72% -> 78% (good)
- warmer traffic hit-rate: 12% -> 6% (bad)
- kv-keys-created-per-min (warmers): 8k -> 22k
- eviction due to ttl: increased 3x
sam: so warmers are polluting the KV namespace and pushing out useful keys?
alex: exactly. autoscaler also picked that up: increased pods to handle added load then scale down -> warmers run again -> oscillation
mira: are warmers running at deploy-time only or cron + autoscale hooks?
denise: we have three paths today: deploy-time synthetic, scheduled prefill (nightly), and on-autoscale opportunistic prefill. warmers tagged with env=synthetic.
sam: thinking out loud — options:
1) attenuate synthetic prefix signal: apply a separate hash namespace + lower priority TTL (so they don't evict real keys)
2) change warmer keying to use controlled prefix templates (less cardinality)
3) run warmers on a separate KV instance/namespace for prefill-only
4) throttle warmers during autoscale events
mira: + run warmers with batching heuristic tuned for long-running throughput (so they pick big-kernel path). Right now kernel_hint:auto misclassifies synthetic short sequences
alex: I prototyped 1 and 2 locally. results: separate namespace cut eviction impact to near-zero and hit-rate for real traffic stayed stable. using controlled templates bumped warmer hit-rate from 6%->40% and reduced keys created by 70%
denise: nice. what's the cost tradeoff? separate namespace means extra mem usage and operational surface. templates might be easiest.
sam: also consider a short cooldown: if autoscaler event detected, pause opportunistic warmers for 5m to avoid feedback loop. simple and low-risk
mira: agreed. proposal: roll out 2-phase plan
- immediate (low effort): change warmer keying to templated prefixes + cooldown on autoscale (can be feature-flagged)
- medium: run warmers in separate KV namespace for 2 weeks of canary traffic to measure cost/benefit
- long-term: add kernel-hint override for warmers so they exercise production kernel selection (and avoid small-kernel path mismatch)
alex: wrote a draft PR that implements templated keying + autoscale cooldown flag. tests include unit for key namespace and a simulation that asserts max new-keys-per-minute bound
```
# example templated prefix
template: "<model>#<intent>#seed_{i}"
```
sam: can you attach the PR? i'll review today. also add a perf job in ci that simulates warmers at 5k qps for 15m
alex: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1427
mira: i'll own the medium plan for the namespace canary. let's schedule a 1hr run in staging next Tue 03:00 UTC. denise please coordinate ops & billing for extra KV during canary
denise: on it. creating infra ticket #INF-2243
deploy-bot: scheduled job: canary-prefill-run -> staging -> Tue 03:00 UTC (id: canary-20260321) :white_check_mark:
alex: sweet. follow-ups: add metric to console: warmer_key_churn, warmer_evictions, warmer_namespace_bytes. we'll track for the canary
sam: going to add alert rule to prevent autoscaler-triggered warmers running for >10m continuous
mira: thanks team — big win if templates + cooldown stop the oscillation without expensive infra changes
denise: quick note: inform customers of possible short-lived prefill instability window during canary? ops says no user-facing impact expected but will post in #incidents if any anomalies
alex: will post a short thread in #eng-notifications before canary. end of thread for now :+1:
